grading_process: Evaluation: 3 Lecture exams (each worth 20% of semester grade) Lab assignments (30% of semester grade) Paper presentation and discussions (10% of semester grade) You will receive one combined grade for your work in lecture and lab for this course. As you can see outlined above, the lab makes up 30% of the final semester grade. However, to pass this course, you must pass both the lecture portion and the lab portion of the course independently. If your performance in either portion of the course is below the required grade to pass the course for the major (C-, or 70%), you would not be able to receive credit for the course. Lab assignments will be discussed in your first lab period. For the lecture, your points come from exams and paper set discussions. You will take 3 non-cumulative exams over the course of the semester (see course schedule). All exams will be taken in class, and all exams must be completed during the first half of the class period (1.5 hours). Exams will be followed by a break and then lecture. Four times during the semester we will discuss some classic articles from the primary literature in ecology. Each student will be responsible for presenting a summary of one or more of the papers and leading a discussion. Each student will receive a grade based on the quality of their presentation and their participation in the discussions throughout the semester. The grade scale is: 94-100%=A; 90-93%=A-; 87-89%=B+; 84-86%=B; 80-83%=B-; 76-79%=C+; 73-75%=C; 70-72%=C- ; 66-69%=D+; 63-65%=D; 60-62%=D; Below 59.99%=F. Attendance: In general, attendance is mandatory because it is strongly correlated with success in this course! This is a fast- paced class, and we will cover a significant amount of content during each meeting. I will take attendance at the start of each class. If you arrive late, you are responsible for checking in with me before leaving class. This is your responsibility. I will not accept emails after class as proof of attendance! You should make every effort to be on time for class because walking in late is disturbing to other students. We understand there may be unavoidable circumstances that prevent you from attending. If you cannot attend a lecture or a lab for any reason, please let us know as far in advance as possible and we will attempt to accommodate you. Classroom behavior You are expected to always conduct yourself in a professional manner while participating in this course. This includes an expectation of respectful behavior during any online or face to face interactions with classmates or me. Regarding cell phones and other electronic devices, please turn off your cell phones in class! If you MUST have your cell phone on because you are expecting an emergency call or need to be available for personal matters, please keep your cell phone on vibrate and leave the room to answer it. If possible, inform me in advance if you are expecting a call and sit on the end of a row so you minimize disturbances to your fellow students! DO NOT TEXT OR ACCESS FACEBOOK OR OTHER SOCIAL MEDIA DURING CLASS. Important Academic Policies Academic Alerts The University is invested in your academic success. If a faculty member is concerned about your academic behavior or performance, they may submit an academic alert. Academic alerts are not punitive. The goal is to provide you with support and resources to support your success. They act as an important check-in point and, if you receive an academic alert, you will receive an email to your UNH email address. It is strongly recommended that you meet with a professional advisor and connect with your instructor to discuss the reason for the alert. Accommodations

Over the course of the semester, it is my aspiration to have students: - Have hands-on experiences with specimen, both living and preserved, that represent various kingdoms of life. - Develop an understanding of phylogeny (the relatedness of different branches of life) - Demonstrate a basic level of proficiency with common lab equipment and techniques, including weighing & measuring, pipetting, safe use of heat sources, aseptic technique, light microscopy and more. - Design experiments including development of hypotheses and integration of adequate controls. - Interpret and analyze scientific data - Communicate their results in the form of graphs, presentations and posters in a way that can be clearly understood by their intended audience. - And enjoy the experience! There may occasionally be extra credit opportunities available to everyone. Assignment descriptions: Lab worksheets (50% of lab grade) – In each lab meeting, you will be provided with worksheets to guide you through the activities. These worksheets should be completed in lab and then relevant sections should be transferred to your digital lab notebook. They will be assessed directly from the digital lab notebook, so you do not need to submit them, unless otherwise directed. Experimental summary assignments (20% of the lab grade) – Over the course of the semester, we will be completing 4 sets of experiments/activities.
